scope: Read-only classification of the completed candidate3 diagnostic baseline; candidate3 failed startup before measurement

evidence.server_queries: server-queries.json: post-load bounded query of system.query_log, query user SELECTs, no SQL text or query ID in captured fields; return code 0, 1621 rows, below 50001-row cap
evidence.harness_events: measurement/harness/events.jsonl: raw HTTP status, route, and request timing
evidence.worker_events: operations/worker.jsonl: 2449 clickhouse_write and 2449 consumer_commit events, no recorded worker errors

contract_and_classification.detector_cap: Incidents SQL uses LIMIT MaxSpans+1; MaxSpans is 100000. Fetching the 100001st deduplicated row returns detector.ErrLimit and the incidents endpoint maps that error to HTTP 503. Successful 100001-row SELECTs are strong evidence that this cap was reached during the baseline measurement, but captured log fields cannot associate a SELECT with a specific HTTP request.
contract_and_classification.other_503_causes: Incident HTTP 503 occurred before the first observed 100001-row SELECT. The same generic HTTP 503 also covers ClickHouse/storage errors, the four-slot query admission cap, response or detector resource caps, and invalid output. Other query routes had 503s and cannot be explained by the incident detector cap.
contract_and_classification.504: Incident HTTP 504 maps context deadline or ClickHouse exception code 159. The captured query-log exception codes 210 and 735 show server-side SELECT exceptions but cannot be mapped to individual HTTP responses; client cancellation after a detector cap or deadline could itself yield such an exception, so these are not independent evidence of a storage outage.
contract_and_classification.transport_and_storage: The worker event stream recorded writes and commits without a worker error. This does not prove individual query failures were caused by the detector; HTTP query transport, API slot admission, and ClickHouse read failures remain separate possible classes.
contract_and_classification.per_request_attribution: unknown: no request ID, SQL text, structured API error cause, or join key links the HTTP event to system.query_log

acceptance_effect: Every non-404 HTTP failure remains in the original query failure gate, including detector input-limit 503s. This evidence explains possible causes but does not waive or reclassify any failure as success. Faster persistence can reach the fixed detector cap sooner; the baseline itself also reached that cap. Candidate3 has no completed diagnostic pair in this probe, so no comparative promotion conclusion follows.
fresh_pair_classification_without_app_im: Keep raw per-route HTTP status/time and the bounded system.query_log SELECT capture for both variants. Classify a 100001-row successful SELECT as detector-cap evidence at the case/time-window level; preserve query-log exception codes separately without inferring their trigger. Correlate timing only as suggestive. Preserve per-request cause as unknown unless an existing response has a distinct cause or a request-to-query join key; report all original failures and thresholds unchanged. The existing candidate2 correlation is additional timing evidence, not per-request proof.
